name: Charles-Édouard Brown-Séquard
contribution: A Franco-Mauritian physiologist and neurologist who, in 1850, became the first to describe what is now called Brown-Séquard syndrome.
legacy: He was the first scientist to work out the physiology of the spinal cord, demonstrating that the decussation of the fibres carrying pain and temperature sensation occurs in the cord itself.

checks.lead: Charles-Édouard Brown-Séquard FRS (8 April 1817 – 2 April 1894) was a Franco-Mauritian physiologist and neurologist who, in 1850, became the first to describe what is now called Brown-Séquard syndrome.
